objective: Stop the 22 ES/FR sibling pages from advertising hreflang=en to a URL that now 301s
mechanismModified: assets/data/seo-pages-manifest.json (removed 11 EN entries for the redirected slugs; ES/FR entries for the same page IDs retained)
assets/data/path-mirror-rows.json (regenerated via scripts/build-path-mirror-rows.mjs from the corrected manifest — 170 rows -> 159 rows)
decisionRationale: Repointing hreflang=en at the new consolidated EN page was considered and rejected: one EN URL cannot correctly declare 7 (or 4) distinct hreflang=es/fr alternates for unrelated ES/FR pages, and validate-arch02.mjs's reciprocity check would have flagged every one of those as non-reciprocal (the new EN page cannot reciprocate to 11 different localized URLs). Since the ES/FR pages' content was not touched in CONTENT-03 (still narrowly scoped to their original topic) there is no genuinely equivalent EN page for them anymore post-consolidation. Removing the stale hreflang=en/x-default-to-EN annotation is the only fix that does not fabricate a false equivalence and does not break reciprocity.
perFileChange: Removed <link rel="alternate" hreflang="en" .../>; repointed hreflang="x-default" from the old EN URL to the page's own canonical URL (self-reference). hreflang="es"/"fr" reciprocal pair between the two sibling files left untouched and still valid (neither of those pages changed).
archO2Result: FULL PASS (10/10 checks) after this fix, unchanged from the already-clean state after 04B — hreflang_issues_audit stayed at 0 throughout (its current design checks alternate-tag presence/reciprocity, not whether a target 301s, so it never flagged this defect; the fix here is a real correction found and verified independent of what this specific automated check happens to catch).
